author: Grace Chen
title: High Cholesterol & Health: Debunking Myths
text:
A widely circulated video making the claim that high cholesterol levels are beneficial for health-even protective against cancer and heart attacks-is demonstrably false, according to leading medical organizations and extensive scientific research. The video, featuring a cardiologist promoting unconventional theories, has sparked concern among health professionals who warn against the spread of misinformation.
The False Claim: Higher Cholesterol, Longer Life?
The central assertion in the video is that individuals with cholesterol levels below 300 mg/dL should be worried, and that higher levels correlate with increased longevity and immunity to serious illnesses. As one source in the video states, “If your cholesterol is below 300, you should be concerned. The higher the cholesterol, the better, as you will live longer. You will never get cancer. Of course, you won’t have a heart attack either.” This claim directly contradicts established medical consensus.
Established Guidelines: Lowering LDL is Key
Current guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology and the European atherosclerosis Society recommend maintaining low levels of LDL cholesterol to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. Numerous studies have shown a clear correlation between high LDL cholesterol and increased risk of heart attack and stroke. Lowering LDL cholesterol through lifestyle changes and, when necessary, medication, is a cornerstone of preventative cardiology.
Debunking the Cancer Myth
The video’s claim that high cholesterol prevents cancer is also demonstrably false. Research from Danish scientists Børge G.Nordestgaard and Martin Bødtker Mortensen shows that high levels of LDL cholesterol, in fact, increase the risk of both heart disease and stroke.Furthermore,high cholesterol can contribute to the progress and progression of tumors by damaging cells and increasing oxidative stress,while cholesterol-lowering drugs like statins may offer a protective effect against cancer.
Statins Under Scrutiny: Balancing Risks and Benefits
The video also alleges that statins are a “diabetic factory,” claiming they cause diabetes in a important percentage of patients and have led to 250,000 new cases in India alone. While it is true that statins can slightly increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes-by approximately 9% according to a meta-analysis of 13 clinical trials involving over 91,000 participants-the benefits of statin therapy in preventing far more serious cardiovascular events far outweigh this risk.Researchers calculated that for every 255 patients taking statins for four years, only one additional case of diabetes might occur. The claim of 250,000 cases in India is not supported by any available data.
Muscle Pain and Statins: A Matter of Degree
The video further asserts that statins cause muscle damage within a week of starting treatment. While myopathy-muscle tissue damage-is a known side effect of statins,it is indeed far less common than suggested. A U.S. study on statin-associated myopathy indicates that symptomatic myopathy occurs in roughly 10-15% of patients, with severe forms (rhabdomyolysis) being extremely rare.Most patients tolerate statins well.
The Source: BM Hegde and Controversial Theories
the individual featured in the video is Belle Monappa Hegde, an Indian cardiologist and former vice-Chancellor of the Manipal Academy of Higher Education. While Dr. hegde advocates for a holistic approach to medicine,integrating modern and alternative treatments,his theories have frequently enough been met with controversy. He has publicly supported the concept of “quantum healing,” which is widely considered pseudoscience by medical experts. In 2023, researchers from IIT-Madras protested his invitation to a lecture, accusing him of promoting “pseudo-science and quackery.”
The Bottom Line: Trust Evidence-Based Medicine
The claim that a cholesterol level above 300 mg/dL prevents cancer and heart attacks is unequivocally false. Medical studies consistently demonstrate that high cholesterol levels increase the risk of heart attack and stroke. There is no evidence to support the notion that high cholesterol protects against cancer; in fact, the opposite is true. While statins may carry a slight risk of increasing diabetes incidence,they remain a crucial tool in preventing far more devastating cardiovascular problems. The statements made in the viral video are not supported by scientific evidence and should not be considered medical advice.
